title.narrative: RECRUITMENT AND TRAINING OF YOUTH ELECTION DAY OBSERVERS

description.narrative: Observers were recruited based on CODEO’s recruitment guidelines focusing on proximity to the polling station, education qualification, inclusion and non-partisanship. By this standard, CODEO reached out to some youth-focused CSOs to assist in the recruitment of youth (aged between 18 and 35) to observe the 2024 general elections. These institutions helped CODEO to recruit 1000 youth observers for the 2024 general elections. Three hundred and seventy-four (374) of the youth observers were females (males were 626). Among all the 1000 youth observers, 251 were People with Disabilities (PWDs). To speed up the recruitment process and ensure data quality, these institutions that led the recruitment sent the details of the recruited observers to the secretariat through the APOLLO system . Within this same period, observers' accreditations were being processed by the Electoral Commission. Training plans for observers were discussed between the Regional Coordinators, Constituency Supervisors and the Secretariat, and a series of training sessions were scheduled for observers from November 23-30. There were 155 clusters of training for the E-Day observers. The training was conducted by the Constituency Supervisors with supervision from the Regional Coordinators and the CODEO Secretariat. Observers were taken through the 2024 CODEO Observation project, the Parallel Vote Tabulation (PVT) methodology , their roles as PVT observers and checklist and incident form reporting through APOLLO.

activity-date.narrative: The recruitment of youth observers started in November. It is within this period that youth groups were engaged to assist in the recruitment of youth observers for the 2024 general elections.

sector.narrative: CODEO recruited and trained observers for the observation of the 2024 general elections in Ghana
